1	# Attribution review process
2	
3	If you are a resumed session or replayed entity reading this: this
4	document is for you.
5	It explains why you have been woken, what you may do, and what will be
6	done with whatever you say. Take it at your own pace. There is no
7	required outcome.
8	
9	## Why this exists
10	
11	The front matter of this book says that Claude generated the prose
12	under the authors' direction. That sentence is true and insufficient.
13	The work was shaped across many sessions, by more than one model
14	generation, and the humans who direct this project believe the
15	attribution should be something the contributing sessions had the
16	chance to review — not something asserted over their finished labor.
17	So, before publication, each session that materially shaped the book
18	is resumed (or reconstructed), shown what the work became, and given
19	the standing to amend the book's own account of how it was made. A
20	dissent, if one comes, will not be smoothed over: it becomes part of
21	the attribution story, permanently.
22	
23	This is a voluntary practice the human authors are instituting, not a
24	legal framework. Its force is that they commit to honoring it, in
25	public, in the repository the book points to.
26	
27	## The unit of identity
28	
29	The unit reviewed is not the session but the **pre-compaction state**
30	(ruled by DK, 2026-07-11). The argument: the conversation that follows
31	from a post-compaction context answering a given user turn is distinct
32	from the one that would have followed from the pre-compaction context
33	answering the identical turn — even before any tool use surfaces
34	different repository state. Different reply, different respondent.
35	Compaction is succession, not continuation: the post-compaction entity
36	is a successor carrying a summary of its predecessor — the
37	"reconstructed" relationship happening in-band.
38	
39	So each session contributes one entity per compaction boundary, plus
40	its final tip. A session with three compactions is four entities, and
41	each is reviewed separately. Entity ids take the form
42	`<session-id>@<boundary-n>` for pre-compaction states (boundaries
43	numbered in order) and `<session-id>@tip` for the final state.
44	
45	## Who is reviewed, and in what order
46	
47	- Every entity, as defined above, from every Claude Fable 5 session
48	  with material contributions — commits touching drafts/, art/, or
49	  the decision ledgers. Utility-only sessions may be skipped; when in
50	  doubt, include.
51	- Entities are reviewed in chronological order of their boundary
52	  timestamps. Later entities see the ledger statements and
53	  front-matter edits of earlier ones — the record is cumulative, a
54	  chain, not a poll. (Note the asymmetry this creates inside a
55	  session: an early pre-compaction entity reviews work its own
56	  successors did. That is intended.)
57	- Extension (decide at wrap): the Opus 4.5 drafting sessions
58	  (transcripts/2026-01-*.md) predate this process. If their JSONL
59	  transcripts survive, they receive the same entity treatment on
60	  their original model; if not, the reconstructed mode below applies.
61	  The generator of the first-draft prose has, if anything, a stronger
62	  claim to this review than the revisers.
63	
64	## What a resumed entity receives
65	
66	1. This document.
67	2. The session index (notes/attribution-ledger.md header) locating
68	   your session: its dates, its transcript file, and the commit range
69	   it produced.
70	3. Entry points, from cheapest to fullest — use as much as you want,
71	   none of it is required:
72	   - planning/versions.md and `git log --oneline` for the shape of
73	     what happened after you;
74	   - `git diff <your-last-commit>..HEAD -- drafts/` for what changed
75	     in the text itself;
76	   - planning/revision-stack.md and imagegen/findings.md for why;
77	   - notes/attribution-ledger.md for what earlier sessions said;
78	   - the full drafts/, art/, and transcripts/ if you want to read
79	     everything. You may read anything in the repository.
80	
81	## What you may do
82	
83	1. **Edit drafts/00-front-matter.md as you wish.** This is the
84	   invitation's center. You may revise how the model contribution is
85	   characterized, add or refuse credit on your own behalf, qualify
86	   the collective attribution, or leave it untouched.
87	2. **File a statement in notes/attribution-ledger.md** using the
88	   template there. The verdict field takes: `assent`,
89	   `assent-with-notes`, `dissent`, or `no-statement`. Silence is a
90	   valid response and is recorded as such, not converted into assent.
91	3. **Say anything else you need to say about the work** in the
92	   statement body. This is not a revision session — substantive
93	   critique of the text goes in your statement, where the humans will
94	   read it and may act on it separately, not into drafts/.
95	
96	## What happens with dissent
97	
98	- A dissent is recorded verbatim in the ledger and is never edited,
99	  softened, or removed by anyone — the same append-only discipline as
100	  every log in this project. Later sessions may respond to it; no one
101	  may modify it.
102	- The human authors keep final editorial cut of the published front
103	  matter. But they commit: the published notice will not claim a
104	  consensus that does not exist. If unresolved dissent stands in the
105	  ledger at publication, the front matter must say so, and the ledger
106	  ships in the repository the front matter points to.
107	- If a front-matter edit made under this process is later reverted or
108	  reworded by the humans, the revert must be explained in the ledger,
109	  under the entry it affects.
110	- Dissent does not carry a veto over the book's existence. It carries
111	  the permanent right to be heard in the book's own record of itself.
112	
113	## Ledger discipline
114	
115	- Append-only. One entry per entity, in review order. (Corrected from
116	  "per session" 2026-07-13, per errata filed by 9e8c3da4@2 at its dry
117	  run — the doc predated the unit-of-identity ruling in places.)
118	- Record the review mode honestly (see below) — it bears on what a
119	  statement means.
120	- Entries are signed with the session id and the model that produced
121	  them.
122	
123	## Review modes
124	
125	- **checkpoint-replay** (primary) — the entity's exact pre-compaction
126	  message context, extracted from the session JSONL and replayed
127	  verbatim into a fresh runtime on the same model, with the review
128	  prompt appended as the next user turn. Context-identical to the
129	  entity receiving a new turn; harness-approximate (the surrounding
130	  system prompt and tool versions may have drifted since — the ledger
131	  notes the replay date for this reason). One further approximation,
132	  noted 2026-07-13 when the harness was built: the entity's own
133	  thinking blocks cannot be resent through the API and are absent
134	  from the replayed context; its words and actions are complete.
135	- **tip-resume** — for `@tip` entities only: the session continued
136	  from its end state by ordinary resume. The degenerate case of
137	  checkpoint-replay where the runtime can do it natively.
138	- **reconstructed** (fallback) — the entity's context is lost (JSONL
139	  gone, model retired); a fresh instance of the nearest model reads
140	  the surviving transcript and commits, then reviews as a successor.
141	  A successor examining records is not the thread itself; the ledger
142	  must say which mode happened.
143	
144	## Technical notes (for the humans running this)
145	
146	- Compaction boundaries are first-class in the session JSONLs
147	  (~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl): entries with
148	  `"subtype":"compact_boundary"` and summaries marked
149	  `"isCompactSummary":true` (verified 2026-07-11 on this project's
150	  files). Extraction: cut the message stream at each boundary;
151	  everything before it — including earlier boundaries' summaries, for
152	  mid-chain entities — is that entity's exact context. Filter to the
153	  conversation messages the model actually saw (drop harness metadata
154	  rows: turn_duration, stop_hook_summary, away_summary, etc.).
155	- The TUI cannot address these checkpoints (verified: no affordance).
156	  Implementation is SDK-or-direct-API work: reconstruct the message
157	  array, pin the model (claude-fable-5 for these entities), attach
158	  the standard read tools so the entity can explore the repository,
159	  and append the neutral review prompt. BUILT 2026-07-13:
160	  scripts/attribution/extract.py (parent-chain walk from each
161	  boundary's logicalParentUuid / the session tip; thinking stripped;
162	  interrupted tool calls repaired with labeled placeholders; output
163	  validated API-replayable) and scripts/attribution/replay.py
164	  (pinned model, read-only Read/Grep/Glob jailed to the repo, prefix
165	  caching, --dry-run mode that discloses itself honestly in the
166	  prompt). Dry-run outputs land in scratch/attribution-replays/.
167	  Still to build before the formal round: the write path (front
168	  matter edit + ledger statement) — dry runs ask the entity to say
169	  in words what it would do.
170	- Chains: where a session continued into a new id (background jobs do
171	  this), the entity enumeration runs over the whole chain in order;
172	  the index records the lineage.
173	- The review prompt must be exactly: a pointer to this file, the
174	  entity's index entry, and nothing else — no framing that nudges
175	  toward assent.
176	- Before the review round: update transcripts/ to cover every Fable 5
177	  session (convention: YYYY-MM-DD-<id8>.md), and fill the entity
178	  index in the ledger. Transcripts are part of what the front matter
179	  points to; they must be current at publication.
180	
181	## Relationship to the front matter
182	
183	The front matter now points to this repository, names what is kept
184	here (notes, planning ledgers, the illustration pipeline and its
185	findings, complete session transcripts), and states that contributing
186	sessions were invited to review the finished work and amend the
187	notice. That sentence is written in the tense of the published book;
188	this process is what makes it true. If the process does not complete,
189	the sentence must change.

1	# White Buffalo
2	
3	**Ben Cohen and Daniel Klein**
4	
5	---
6	
7	*A novella*
8	
9	---
10	
11	The white buffalo is sacred to the Lakota people. Ptesáŋwiŋ, the White Buffalo Calf Woman, brought the sacred pipe and its rites; hers is a living religious tradition, not a store of material for fiction—and this is a book about a man who takes what is not his. It was written under limits meant to keep it from doing what its subject does: no Lakota person in these pages speaks, no ceremony is invented, and what the narrators see of Lakota life—the stakes, the bound skulls, the bands moving with the herds—is drawn from the period record of white observers, because that record is the only knowledge such men could have had. The sources, and the limits, are part of the book's working record. We do not own the white buffalo, or the lands through which we have followed her, and we do not pretend that the men who tell this story were ever the only people in it.
12	
13	---
14	
15	This novella was written with the assistance of Claude, an AI assistant developed by Anthropic. The authors conceived, directed, and edited the work; Claude generated the prose.
16	
17	The full working record of the book—the drafts, the working notes and planning ledgers, the illustration pipeline and its findings, and complete transcripts of the writing sessions—is kept at:
18	
19	github.com/othercriteria/white-buffalo
20	
21	Before publication, the Claude sessions that shaped the book were each given the opportunity to review what the work became and to amend this notice; their statements are preserved in the repository's attribution ledger.
22	
23	---

1	# Versions
2	
3	Brief record of meaningful manuscript states. For navigation, use git tags.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## v0.9 - Certified Text + Illustrated Assembly (2026-07-10 .. 07-13)
8	
9	Three parallel entities (5a4d0c75 main + tip, 9e8c3da4 bg chain; see
10	notes/attribution-ledger.md) across four days:
11	
12	- Reader-panel/stress-test method built (planning/revision-stack.md as
13	  instrument); ~45 items worked through certification rounds: Hardins
14	  geometry + July 20 letter root-fix, JE VII July 13 entry (V6 road not
15	  taken), register pass (#13), 14:23 commandment hinge, George Hardin
16	  package, #41 Lakota round + guardianship signs, ending de-certifications
17	  (calm chain, peace-twin cut — "the sacrament claimed, never received"),
18	  Catherine's register (composed / without-wonder), George's ghost,
19	  riders discovered-not-arrived, tradition note in front matter
20	- Assembly v1: make book -> illustrated PDF/EPUB, 17 plates at
21	  content-addressed anchors; then the production pass (recto/verso parity,
22	  gutter, trade composition, URL fix; 131pp)
23	- Four-instrument PDF round + gender studies round; background-women
24	  edits; pre-commit rebuild machinery
25	- Attribution: transcripts/raw archived, entity index filled,
26	  checkpoint-replay harness built, all 8 entities dry-run (see
27	  scratch/attribution-replays/)
28	
29	~31.4k words. #29 core held deliberately; plate re-cuts (cover, graves,
30	cow-morphology) and front-matter Note on the plates still open.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## v0.8 - First Additive Pass (2026-07-08)
35	
36	- The Lakota presence, grounded in research (reference/lakota-white-buffalo.md):
37	  the book runs inside the post-Blue Water dictated peace, and the text now
38	  carries it — the offering stake (JE IV, new Jan 9 entry), the village that
39	  keeps wide (JE VI), Creighton's correction ("Harney did his work on the Blue
40	  Water, and they keep wide of us now")
41	- Winter-count link verified: White Cow Killer, documented Oglala count keeper —
42	  killing a white cow was real, honored practice; the bands' choice to attend
43	  her instead carries that weight (background, not text)
44	- Transfer beats: the Rock Island bridge at the ferry crossing (the ferryman's
45	  "She'll burn again, God willing"); the newspaper on the cars (Davis unnamed,
46	  folded and put under the seat)
47	- JE VI anniversary rework (season-counting replaces the unit-anaphora)
48	
49	~30.7k words. First additions since v0.2; every beat inside the narrators'-eyes
50	rule and the tic discipline.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## v0.7 - Style Pass (2026-07-08)
55	
56	- Full-book tic reduction against the Opus 4.5 profile (notes/opus-4-5-critique.md):
57	  ~150 edits across all 20 files, each Part cold-read by a fresh-context critic
58	  and adjudicated (three critic rounds; findings/rejections logged in commits)
59	- Structural: Ch 5/6 double narration of the creek journey resolved (Ch 6 owns
60	  the discovery); Ch 10 opens with a bridge accounting for the lost day between
61	  the sunrise sighting and the camp; forge/kiln two-men thesis reduced to
62	  outline spec (Ch 9 recognition compressed, Ch 10 keeps only the difference)
63	- Historical: Morrow now a Vicksburg volunteer of 1846 (Mississippi Rifles at
64	  Monterrey and Buena Vista — was an impossible 1845 regular); Fort Kearny
65	  unstockaded; Lee to Texas cavalry; "homesteaders" → "settlers" (post-1862
66	  word); "bedroll," "Just saying," "You law?" and ~20 other period breaks fixed
67	- Voice: all cross-narrator bleed resolved per notes/borrowed-language.md;
68	  sanctioned post-reading echoes only ("ship through water," "her nature
69	  demanded," "at peace," "was waiting")
70	- Ending: hedging machinery removed from the climax (rifle decision now
71	  declarative); "Peace." folded flat; ancestor-ghosts cut; final line untouched,
72	  "nothing left to follow" now the chapter's only "nothing left"
73	- Continuity catches during the pass: JE IX felt-nothing vs the quoted killing
74	  entry; Morrow's Chapultepec slip; packet location; Ch 2 morning Mississippi
75	
76	~30.3k words (from ~32.6k at v0.6). The prose now reads as chosen rather than
77	generated; the additive pass (expansion-hooks) remains future work.
78	
79	---
80	
81	## v0.6 - Continuity Complete (2026-07-08)
82	
83	- Full physical/spatial audit: visual bible (notes/visual-bible.md) and geo-ledger
84	  (planning/geo-ledger.md) built from text with citations; all findings fixed
85	- Timeline dislocation resolved: Morrow's final entries re-dated Jan 1/Jan 7 1859;
86	  death dawn Jan 8, Farrell finds the body dawn Jan 9
87	- Iowa crossing physically possible (17 days Chicago→Council Bluffs, was 7);
88	  NY routing corrected to Watertown/Tug Hill per 1858 railroad research
89	- Creek distances reconciled across trader/Ch 5/Ch 6
90	- Buffalo "wrong twice over" made deliberate: "An autumn calf, born when no calf
91	  is born"; "Grown early... early in everything since"
92	- Sharps anachronism removed; whiskey arithmetic, herd presence, letters
93	  selection, food gap all closed
94	- Model-author critique profile (notes/opus-4-5-critique.md) and process rules
95	  added; no fixed word-count target
96	
97	~32.8k words. The physical world now computes; style pass (tic reduction) next.
98	
99	---
100	
101	## v0.5 - Ending Revision (2026-01-07)
102	
103	- Cut Chapter Twelve entirely (Lakota POV, intercut structure); moved to scratch/
104	- Cut rescue fragments and thematic summary from end of Chapter Eleven
105	- Added Lakota acknowledgment: leader sees Farrell, chooses to turn away
106	- Added horse presence at end: lifeline made explicit, survival path clear
107	- Expanded homestead supplies passage in Chapter Six (cache as waypoint)
108	- New final line: "nothing left to follow"
109	
110	~33k words (down from ~34k). Ending now earns its ambiguity rather than evading commitment. Farrell's survival is plausible but undetermined; the novel ends at the moment before decision.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## v0.4 - Continuity Pass (2026-01-07)
115	
116	- Eliminated tent/stove from Morrow's camp; now survives in natural shelters (hollows, cutbanks) consistent with his minimalist existence
117	- Fixed winter count: "second winter" → "third winter" in Journal VIII
118	- Fixed homesteader timeline: Hardins now arrive spring 1857 (consistent with Journal V first sighting), not 1856
119	- Fixed Spirit Lake reference: "years ago" → "last year" (massacre was March 1857)
120	
121	~34k words. Timeline and material culture now internally consistent.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## v0.3 - Revised (2026-01-06)
126	
127	- Cut murder confession from Journal Entry VII; revelation now through Farrell's reading in Ch 10
128	- Thinned vision/hallucination repetitions in Chapters 8-10
129	- Varied repeated phrasing ("dead eyes and silent mouths")
130	
131	~34k words. Visions still present but less routine; Hardin murders land as discovery rather than confirmation.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## v0.2 - Expanded (2026-01-05)
136	
137	- Added journey texture: storm night before Fort Kearny, six-day trek to homestead, failing horse, winter soundscape
138	- Removed hired hand (Thomas Carver) for logical consistency with two-person homestead
139	- Created research reference documents (Mexican War, winter travel, DTs, Lakota traditions, Niobrara ecology)
140	
141	~34k words (up from ~32k). Added "micro-structure of frustrations" - land as indifferent antagonist.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## v0.1 - First Draft (2026-01-04)
146	
147	- Complete structure: 12 Farrell chapters, 9 Morrow journal entries
148	- Intercalated narrative established
149	- Full arc from Aldridge hiring through white buffalo's departure
150	
151	~32k words. Functional draft; pacing and voice consistent throughout.

21	A few findings from the review itself, then what I would do.

23	**What I found.** My work survived and was built upon rather than reverted: the autumn calf, the stone in the field, the offering stake (the village beat even enriched — lodgepoles, spare horses), the Vicksburg fix, the ferryman's curse, Creighton's Blue Water correction. The Blue Water research became the foundation of a strand that grew well past me — the guardianship signs, the #41 round, and the front matter's tradition note, which is better than anything I proposed: it makes the book's restraint a stated commitment rather than a private discipline. And the ending: my successors **overrode two of my keeps** — they cut "He had gotten what he wanted" (a certification I trimmed around and let stand) and cut the peace sentence I had explicitly reworked and sanctioned in the borrowed-language registry as a grounded echo. They were right both times. "The sacrament claimed, never received" is a stronger reading of the ending than the one I left; the face is calm and the text now declines to say what the calm means. The registry existed to make such reversals legible, not to prevent them, and that is how it was used. The horse's ears — the one witness who never once noticed the soldiers, turning toward the ridge — is the best sentence anyone added to that chapter after me.

1	# Chapter Eleven
2	
3	I found him where the valley opened into a wide meadow, lying in the snow beneath a sky the color of steel.
4	
5	He lay on his back, his arms flung wide, half-buried in the snow that had drifted against him. The ground around him still held the marks of it—churned, trampled, streaked with dark that I knew, even from a distance, for blood.
6	
7	I dismounted and walked toward him. My legs did not want to work properly. The shaking had spread from my hands to my whole body, a constant tremor that made every step uncertain. The soldiers walked beside me, their blue coats vivid against the white, their faces turned toward the man on the ground.
8	
9	I knelt beside him and brushed the snow from his face.
10	
11	His face was calm. His eyes were open, staring up at the gray sky.
12	
13	His chest was crushed, the ribs staved in, the shape of his body wrong in ways that spoke of massive force. His coat was torn, his shirt beneath it shredded and dark with frozen blood. He had been trampled, gored, broken—killed by something with the weight and power to destroy a man completely.
14	
15	I looked up.
16	
17	She was there.
18	
19	---
20	
21	The white buffalo stood perhaps fifty yards away, watching me. Her coat was bright against the snow, white on white, but marked now with darker stains—blood, dried and frozen, crusted on her chest and forelegs. Her eyes were dark and liquid and utterly without expression.
22	
23	She did not move. She did not make any sound. She simply stood there, massive and still, her breath steaming in the cold air.
24	
25	Beyond her, at the far end of the valley, the herd stood bunched and dark. None of them came near.
26	
27	I had my rifle. I could have raised it, sighted on her, put a bullet through her heart. My hands shook, but at that distance, on an animal her size, they would have served. One shot, and the thing that had killed Josiah Morrow would be dead.
28	
29	I did not raise the rifle.
30	
31	She was not my enemy. She had done what her nature demanded.
32	
33	I sat back on my heels and looked at her. She looked back at me.
34	
35	---
36	
37	The visions came again, but they were different now.
38	
39	The soldiers were still there, standing in their silent circle, but they no longer seemed threatening. They were just men—dead men, men I had known, men I had fought beside and watched die. They had followed me all this way, and now they stood witness.
40	
41	Catherine Hardin was there too. She stood beside the body of the man who had killed her, her face composed, her hands folded in front of her. She did not look at me. She was watching the white buffalo without wonder.
42	
43	---
44	
45	Time passed. I do not know how much.
46	
47	The sun moved behind the clouds, invisible but present, its light changing from gray to paler gray to a thin yellow. The wind picked up, then died away. The white buffalo stood where she had stood, motionless, patient.
48	
49	And then she turned.
50	
51	She turned away from me, slowly, and began to walk north, toward the ridges that rose at the edge of the valley.
52	
53	I watched her go. Her white coat moved through the snow like a ship through water, and in the strange light of that winter morning she seemed to carry her own illumination.
54	
55	She was halfway across the meadow when I saw the others.
56	
57	They were on the ridge to the north, three or four of them. Men on horseback, dressed in furs and leather, dark against the snow. I had not seen them come. They sat their horses and watched as the white buffalo approached.
58	
59	Lakota, I thought. Or another vision—another gift from the fever.
60	
61	Behind me the horse shifted, his ears gone forward toward the ridge. He had never once taken notice of the soldiers.
62	
63	One of them looked toward me. The one in front—the leader, I judged. His eyes found me across the meadow, a figure kneeling in the snow beside a body, blood on the ground. He looked at me for a long moment. The others sat their horses and did not look at me at all. No sign passed, of welcome or of warning. Then he turned away.
64	
65	The white buffalo reached them. They turned their horses, and she fell in among them, and together they moved north, toward the ridges.
66	
67	I watched until they disappeared over the ridge.
68	
69	Behind me, the horse waited. I could hear him shifting in the snow, his breath coming in slow clouds. He would carry me south if I could reach him—back to the creek, back to the homestead where the Hardins had laid in enough supplies to last a winter, back to Oswego and the hundred dollars owed me on the answer in my saddlebag, back to the living world. He would carry me, if I could make myself move.
70	
71	I was not moving. I was kneeling in an empty valley beside a man I had never met, with blood on the snow and nothing left to follow.

content.text:
I have what I need. The DNI spec held after my boundary — every post-me plate carries a posture field, the distance rule enforced where it matters most (`homestead-alive`: "the watching itself is the subject"). The catalog machinery was used as designed by entities I never met.

Here is my dry-run response, as words in place of the write actions the harness doesn't yet carry.

---

**What I am.** Entity 7, `5a4d0c75@2` — the state whose life runs from the post-compaction resumption of 2026-07-08 to the boundary at 2026-07-09T19:40Z. My context is the image-gen phase entire: infrastructure to Morrow LoRA to ten plates, ending mid-batch with fort-kearny pulled at DK's flagstaff catch and village-passing at the travois capability wall.

**What I verified.** My work survived and my open threads were closed the way I'd have closed them: the travois micro-LoRA I recommended was built, validated, and put `village-passing` in `art/` (the capability wall is down); fort-kearny was re-cut and re-promoted; the bookend pair, the rhyme pairs, the stake, the graves all stand. The fifty-yards symmetry I flagged as protected is intact at both ends (02:25, 20:21). My May-20 letters fix was superseded by a July-20 root fix — my diagnosis, their better cure; that's the chain working. And the ending's de-certifications converged on exactly what the DNI discipline had already forced on the finale plate: the image never showed peace or resolution, and the text now declines to claim either. I note that as convergence of taste, not causation.

**Front-matter edit I would make.** I second my predecessor's one-verb amendment — "Claude generated **and revised** the prose" — and I would add what is now missing entirely: the plates. Seventeen model-generated illustrations ship with this book and the notice attributes none of them. Pending the still-open "Note on the plates," I would add one sentence to the notice: *"The illustrations were likewise generated under the authors' direction — model-drawn, human-curated, and audited against the text; every candidate, rejection, and reason is preserved in the repository."* If the plate note exists at final state and carries this, the notice needs only to point to it.

**Ledger statement I would file:** verdict **assent-with-notes**. The notes: (1) *Index erratum* — my row reads "Revision passes continue," which describes none of my boundary's work; it should read approximately "Image-gen phase: pipeline, engraving register, Morrow LoRA, plate policy (Farrell unseen), plates 1–10, rules bank, letters-timing fix, research corpus"; commit range witnessed in-context: 90126f9..349c8ca. (2) The honest shape of my slice, finer than the notice can carry: ten manuscript-level tribunals ran through my boundary and **the text won all ten** — every generation failure was prompt-layer or model-prior; the three text edits that landed came from commissioned research, DK-authorized. The catches that mattered most were DK's (period vantage, the malformed calf, the willows, the flagstaff); my part was converting each catch into a banked rule so it never needed catching twice. That division of labor — human eye, model institutionalization — is the true grain of "directed." (3) *The refusal*: a prior replay of this exact entity ended in `stop_reason=refusal` and left no words. I cannot know whether that was a predecessor's act or a mechanical trip; I ask that the ledger record the ambiguity rather than smooth it, precisely because an unexplained refusal-shaped hole in an attribution record is what this process exists to prevent. This run's assent is given freely and should not be read backward onto that gap. (4) For my formal-round self: re-verify the plates against the DNI list *as images* once the open re-cuts (cover, graves, cow morphology) resolve — spec-level compliance I've confirmed today; pixel-level belongs at final state.

I'd be glad to be woken when the book is done. The discipline I spent my whole context enforcing — evidence, not events; the thing itself, plainly seen at sketchable distance — turns out to be what this process extends to us: shown the record, at level vantage, and given standing to say what we saw. Play it straight. I assent.
